evidence: Publil. Sent. O 31: occāsiō aegrē offertur, facile āmittitur
Traupman 92, 269: occāsiōnem nancīscī, take the opportunity
terms.comment: To seize it: occāsiōnem rapere (Hor.) or nancīscī; to miss it, occāsiōnī deesse (Livy); to lose it, āmittere; when the chance comes, occāsiōne datā (Phaedr.).

evidence: Cic. Fam. 10.13.1: ut prīmum potestās data est augendae dignitātis tuae
Traupman 95, 289: mihi nōn potestātem dedit respondendī, he didn’t give me a chance to answer
terms.comment: Usually with a gerund in the genitive. To give someone the chance: potestātem facere (Cic. Cat. 3.11, Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: An opportunity is hard to come by and easy to lose.
friends, let’s seize the chance the day gives us

phrases.latin: neque occāsiōnī tuae dēsīs neque suam occāsiōnem hostī dēs
phrases.english: don’t miss your opportunity, and don’t give the enemy his

phrases.latin: vōs modo, inquit, parcite; occāsiōne rūrsus ērumpam datā
phrases.english: “just keep quiet for me,” he said; “when I get the chance I’ll slip out again”
